definition: The 18 m by 9 m playing area. The net splits it into two 9 m by 9 m halves, one per team.
example: Each team defends its own half of the court.

definition: The line under the net that splits the court into two halves.
example: A foot may cross the centre line only if part of it stays on or above the line.

definition: The line 3 m from the centre line on each side. It separates the front zone from the back zone.
example: A back-row player must take off from behind the attack line to attack above the net.

definition: The area between the centre line and the attack line.
example: Back-row players may not complete an attack above the net from the front zone.

definition: The area behind the attack line, up to the end line.
example: The libero usually plays in the back zone.

definition: The line at the back of each half of the court.
example: The server must not touch the end line when hitting the serve.

definition: The two lines along the long sides of the court.
example: A ball that lands on the sideline is in.

definition: The 9 m wide area behind the end line where the server stands.
example: The server can serve from anywhere inside the service zone.

definition: The space around the court where players may still play the ball.
example: A player can chase a ball into the free zone and send it back.

definition: The barrier across the middle of the court. The ball must go over it, between the antennae.
example: Touching the net between the antennae while playing the ball is a fault.

definition: 2.43 m for men and 2.24 m for women in senior play.
example: Youth and recreational leagues often use a lower net.

definition: A flexible rod fixed to each side of the net. It marks the side edge of the space the ball must cross.
example: A ball that touches the antenna is out.

definition: The part of the vertical plane of the net, between the antennae and below the ceiling, that the ball must pass through to go to the other side.
example: A ball that goes outside the antenna has not crossed in the crossing space.

definition: The six areas of each half, numbered 1 to 6. With the net at the top, the front row is 4, 3, 2 and the back row is 5, 6, 1.
example: Zone 1 is the right back, where the server starts.

definition: The three players in zones 4, 3 and 2 at the serve. They may block and attack from anywhere.
example: When the setter is in the front row, there are only two front-row hitters.

definition: The three players in zones 5, 6 and 1 at the serve. They may not block, and must attack from behind the attack line.
example: A back-row player who jumps from behind the attack line may attack above the net.

definition: The player who usually takes the second contact and sets the ball up for a hitter.
example: In a 5-1, one setter sets in all six rotations.

definition: A player who attacks mainly from the left side (zone 4) and helps pass the serve.
example: Teams usually have two outside hitters across from each other in the lineup.

definition: A player who blocks at the centre of the net and attacks quick sets.
example: The libero often replaces the middle blocker in the back row.

definition: The player across the lineup from the setter. They attack mainly from the right side.
example: In a 5-1, the opposite is always three zones away from the setter.

definition: A back-row defensive specialist in a different coloured jersey. The libero may only play in the back row and may not block, attempt to block or serve.
example: The libero comes in for the middle blocker when the middle rotates to the back row.

definition: A substitute who comes in to pass and defend. Unlike the libero, they follow normal substitution rules.
example: A coach may sub in a defensive specialist for a front-row hitter who rotates to the back.

definition: The player who speaks for the team with the referees.
example: Only the game captain may ask the referee to explain a call during play.

definition: The starting order of the six players, recorded on the line-up sheet before each set. It stays the same for the whole set.
example: A lineup of S, OH1, MB1, OPP, OH2, MB2 puts the setter in zone 1.

definition: Moving one zone clockwise when your team wins the serve back. The player who moves from zone 2 to zone 1 serves next.
example: After a side-out, everyone rotates before the next serve.

definition: The order set by the lineup, which players must keep at the moment of the serve (receiving team).
example: Under FIVB rules, only the receiving team must be in rotational order at the serve.

definition: Being out of place relative to a neighbour at the serve, such as a back-row player standing ahead of the front-row player in front of them.
example: The player in zone 6 must be behind the player in zone 3 when the ball is served.

definition: A player is not in their correct position when the ball is served. The other team gets the point and the serve.
example: Standing ahead of your front-row teammate at the serve is a positional fault.

definition: Serving out of the rotation order. The other team gets the point and the serve.
example: If the wrong player serves, it is a rotational fault.

definition: Replacing one player with another during a set. Libero replacements do not count as substitutions.
example: A team gets a limited number of regular substitutions each set.

definition: When the libero swaps in or out for a back-row player. Replacements are unlimited and are not counted as substitutions.
example: The libero replaces the middle blocker after the middle serves or rotates out.

definition: Moving to your playing spot right after the serve. It is legal because players may move anywhere once the ball is served.
example: The setter switches to the right front after the serve to set.

definition: Arranging players at the serve so they can switch quickly while still staying in legal order.
example: Teams often stack the setter close to the right side in serve receive.

definition: Where a player goes after the serve to play their role.
example: A setter's base position is the right front, between zones 2 and 3.

definition: The hit that puts the ball into play, made by the right-back player from the service zone.
example: The server has 8 seconds after the whistle to serve.

definition: The player who serves: whoever is in zone 1 when the rally starts.
example: After a side-out, the player who rotates into zone 1 becomes the server.

definition: The order in which players serve, which follows the lineup.
example: Serving out of order is a rotational fault.

definition: The server must hit the ball within 8 seconds of the first referee's whistle.
example: Taking too long to serve gives the point to the other team.

definition: A serve hit while jumping, usually with topspin and power.
example: The server may land inside the court after hitting a jump serve.

definition: A serve hit with little or no spin, so it moves unpredictably in the air.
example: A good float serve can be hard to pass because it wobbles.

definition: A serve hit from below the waist with an open hand or fist. It is legal in all levels of play.
example: Many new players start with an underhand serve.

definition: A serve that scores directly, with no successful pass by the receiving team.
example: The server earned an ace when the ball dropped between two passers.

definition: A serve that lands out, fails to cross the net, or touches an antenna. The other team scores.
example: Hitting the serve into the net is a service error.

definition: When players of the serving team block the receivers' view of the server or the ball's path. It is a fault.
example: Teammates bunching up in front of the server to hide the serve can be called for a screen.

definition: A serve that touches the net and still goes over. It is in play.
example: The net serve trickled over and the receivers had to scramble.

definition: Any touch of the ball by a player.
example: A team may make up to three contacts before sending the ball over.

definition: A team may touch the ball up to three times before it must cross the net. A block does not count as one of the three.
example: Pass, set, hit is the classic three-contact play.

definition: A team touching the ball four times before sending it over. It is a fault.
example: Pass, set, hit, then one more touch before the ball crosses is four hits.

definition: One player touching the ball twice in a row, or the ball touching several parts of their body one after another. It is a fault, except at the block and on the first team contact in one action.
example: A setter who touches the ball twice in a row has made a double contact.

definition: When the ball is caught or thrown instead of being hit. It is a fault.
example: A tip that is held in the hand before being pushed over is a catch.

definition: A player using a teammate or any object to reach the ball. It is a fault.
example: Pushing off a teammate to jump higher for a dig is an assisted hit.

definition: Usually the first contact, sending the ball to the setter.
example: A good pass lets the setter choose any hitter.

definition: Playing the ball off the forearms held together. Often called a bump.
example: Most serves are received with a forearm pass.

definition: Playing the ball above the head with the fingers of both hands.
example: Setters use an overhead pass to set the ball.

definition: The contact that places the ball for a teammate to attack, usually the second contact.
example: A high set to the outside gives the hitter time to approach.

definition: Any action that sends the ball toward the opponent, except a serve or a block.
example: A spike, a tip and a roll shot are all attack hits.

definition: A powerful attack hit from above the net.
example: The outside hitter spiked the ball cross-court for a kill.

definition: A soft attack pushed over or around the block with the fingertips. It must not be caught or thrown.
example: A tip into the middle of the court can catch the defence off guard.

definition: An attack hit with a slow, looping arm swing so the ball drops behind the block.
example: The hitter used a roll shot over the block into zone 6.

definition: An attack hit from a standing position or a small jump, used when a full spike is not possible.
example: After a poor pass, the hitter sent a down ball deep to zone 1.

definition: An attack that ends the rally in the attacking team's favour.
example: The middle blocker scored a kill on a quick set.

definition: A pass of a hard-driven attack, usually close to the floor.
example: The libero dug the spike and kept the rally alive.

definition: Players close to the net reaching above it to stop the opponent's attack. Only front-row players may complete a block, and a block touch does not count as a team contact.
example: After a block touch, the team still has three contacts.

definition: A back-row player or the libero completing or attempting a block. It is a fault.
example: The setter in zone 1 may not join the block.

definition: A blocker may reach beyond the net, but must not touch the ball on the opponent's side before or during the opponent's attack hit.
example: Blocking a ball the hitter has already attacked is legal even if your hands are over the net.

definition: When players from both teams contact the ball above the net at the same time. Play continues.
example: After the joust, the ball fell on the blue team's side, so they kept playing it.

definition: An attack hit off the block so it lands out of bounds. The point goes to the attacking team.
example: The hitter tooled the block and the ball landed out past the sideline.

definition: Teammates moving close to their own attacker to dig a ball that is blocked back.
example: Good cover turned the blocked spike into a second attack.

definition: An easy ball sent over without an attack, often with a forearm pass.
example: On a free ball, blockers drop back from the net to get ready to attack.

definition: A pass that goes straight over the net, giving the opponent an easy attack.
example: A hard serve forced an overpass, and the front row hit it straight down.

definition: Switching from defence to attack, or back, during a rally.
example: After the dig, the team transitioned and the setter ran in to set.

definition: An attack by a back-row player. It is legal only if the player takes off from behind the attack line when the ball is fully above the net.
example: The opposite hit a back-row attack from behind the attack line.

definition: A back-row attack from the middle of the court, around zone 6.
example: The outside hitter ran a pipe while the front row distracted the block.

definition: A fast, low set to the middle blocker, who is already in the air.
example: The middle hit a quick set before the block could form.

definition: The setter attacks the second ball instead of setting it. A back-row setter may not complete this attack from in front of the attack line with the ball fully above the net.
example: A front-row setter can dump the ball over when the block is not ready.

definition: The play from the serve until the ball is out of play.
example: The rally ended when the ball landed in.

definition: Every rally scores a point, whichever team served.
example: With rally scoring, a mistake on your own serve still gives the other team a point.

definition: Winning the rally while receiving. The receiving team scores and earns the serve.
example: A side-out means your team rotates before serving.

definition: A game within a match, won by the first team to 25 points with a two-point lead.
example: The team won the first set 25 to 22.

definition: A contest of up to five sets. The first team to win three sets wins the match.
example: The match went to five sets.

definition: The fifth set, played to 15 points with a two-point lead.
example: In the deciding set, teams switch sides at 8 points.

definition: A 30-second break requested by a team. Each team may take up to two per set.
example: The coach called a timeout to reset after three straight points.

definition: A rally played again, for example when both teams commit faults at the same time.
example: After a double fault, the referee called for a replay.

definition: When both teams commit a fault at the same time. The rally is replayed.
example: Both players touching the net at once is a double fault.

definition: Touching the net between the antennae while playing the ball. Touching it when not playing the ball is not a fault, as long as it does not interfere with play.
example: Brushing the top of the net while blocking is a net fault.

definition: Crossing into the opponent's court in a way that is not allowed, such as with the whole foot or by interfering with their play.
example: Landing with your whole foot past the centre line is a fault.

definition: A ball that lands on or inside the boundary lines. The lines are part of the court.
example: The ball clipped the end line, so it was in.

definition: A ball that lands outside the lines, touches an antenna, or hits something outside the court such as the ceiling or a wall.
example: The serve hit the ceiling, so it was out.

definition: A call that means "I will take this ball," so teammates do not collide.
example: Call "Mine!" early on every pass you take.

definition: A call that the opponent is about to send an easy ball over.
example: When the other team only bumps it over, call "Free!" and drop off the net.

definition: The formation the receiving team uses to pass the serve.
example: In serve receive, the setter is often stacked near the right side.

definition: A system with one setter in all six rotations and five hitters: two outside hitters, two middle blockers and one opposite.
example: In a 5-1, the setter is across the lineup from the opposite.

definition: A system with two setters, each setting only from the back row, so there are always three front-row hitters.
example: In a 6-2, the setter who rotates to the front row becomes a hitter.

definition: A system with two setters, each setting from the front row, and four hitters. Common with newer teams.
example: A 4-2 keeps things simple, but only two players attack in each rotation.

definition: A back-row setter running forward to the net right after the serve to set.
example: When the setter is in zone 1, they penetrate to the right front to set.

definition: The official on the stand at one end of the net who starts each rally and has the final say.
example: The first referee whistles for the serve.

definition: The official on the floor across from the first referee who watches the net, the centre line and substitutions.
example: The second referee called the net fault.
